title: Iron Man
synopsis: After captors use weapons made by his company, Tony Stark escapes and reconsiders what he owes the people his business has injured.
verdictRationale: Yinsen’s sacrifice and Tony’s decision to stop building weapons give the story moral weight. Its sexual humor and sustained spectacle make the overall recommendation Neutral.
ageRationale: Gunfire, captivity and injuries are intense. There is a brief implied sexual encounter and drinking.

themes.name: Responsibility

themes.evidence: Tony’s confidence in his company’s work is shaken by what he sees during captivity.

themes.name: Sexual content
themes.evidence: Tony and a reporter kiss and tumble into bed, with sex implied.

themes.name: LGBTQ Themes & Messaging
themes.evidence: On the jet, Tony makes a brief joke about Rhodey mistaking someone’s gender during a spring-break encounter. The clip establishes the dialogue, with no identity established for the person mentioned.

warnings.name: Sexual content

warnings.name: Language

warnings.name: Drinking and substance use

reflection: Repentance begins with seeing whose burdens we have ignored. Tony’s decision to halt production gives a family room to discuss what making amends would mean beyond a public announcement.

themeScripture.connection: Paul calls Christians to consider the interests of others. Tony’s change invites us to ask who bears the cost of our choices and what repair asks of us.
themeScripture.text: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.

title: The Incredible Hulk

verdictRationale: Betty’s care and the Hulk’s final restraint give families something to discuss. Prolonged destructive combat competes with that emphasis.
ageRationale: Monster fights, bloody wounds, loud explosions and a passionate hotel-room scene make this more suitable for teens.

title: Thor

ageRationale: Fantasy battles, threatening creatures, some profanity and bar drinking support a teen recommendation.
